recent_posts.title: CSS { In Real Life }
recent_posts.summary: Modern web experiences have become cluttered with JavaScript-heavy pages, intrusive pop-ups, and poor UX design, driving users toward AI chatbots as an alternative to traditional web browsing. The author draws parallels between Adobe Acrobat's messy interface and the current state of websites, arguing that improving web usability could reduce demand for AI-powered browsing solutions despite their accuracy and ethical concerns.

recent_posts.title: Reflections From Green IO 2025
recent_posts.summary: Green IO 2025 conference focused on sustainable technology and responsible development practices. Key themes included AI's massive energy consumption impact, innovative solutions like using data center heat for home heating, government digital sustainability initiatives, and tools for carbon-aware computing. Speakers emphasized starting sustainability efforts from current positions rather than waiting for perfect solutions, while highlighting the interconnected nature of environmental and social issues in technology.

recent_posts.title: Creating CSS Theme Variables from a JS file
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to define brand colors and their variants in a JavaScript file and generate corresponding CSS custom properties automatically using a Node.js script. This approach ensures consistency and reduces maintenance by keeping theme variables centralized. The guide covers the setup of a Node.js project, writing a script to map JS object keys to CSS properties, and exporting the generated CSS to a file.

recent_posts.title: Wholegrain Digital’s Response to the BBC’s Web Sustainability Report
recent_posts.summary: Wholegrain Digital responds to the BBC's report on digital sustainability, which criticizes some community-developed web sustainability guidelines. The response emphasizes the importance of collaboration and evolving evidence in creating guidelines to minimize the environmental impact of websites.

recent_posts.title: Debating the Merits of LLMs
recent_posts.summary: The post debates the ethical implications of utilizing large language models (LLMs) like GPT-4 and Claude. While some argue that LLMs could potentially advance scientific endeavors, the post emphasizes that LLMs are primarily for text synthesis, not scientific discovery. It also points out that AI can be useful in specific industrial applications, but should not be confused with the capabilities of LLMs. The post encourages scrutiny on the value and ethics of LLM use, especially outside of specific professional contexts.

recent_posts.title: What I learned from migrating a Vue project from Vuex to Pinia
recent_posts.summary: Migrating from Vuex to Pinia in a Vue web app offers insights into both technical and non-technical aspects. Key reasons, methods for conducting such a migration, and tips specific to switching from Vuex to Pinia are discussed to guide large web project migrations.

recent_posts.title: Creating Static SVGs from GeoJSON
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to convert GeoJSON map data into static SVG files using the D3.js library. This post offers a step-by-step guide to fetching GeoJSON data, creating SVG elements, and scaling geographic features correctly within the SVG viewBox. It also addresses common issues and explores server-side SVG generation using Node.js.

recent_posts.title: Sustainable phone choices and eco-friendly practices
recent_posts.summary: The author shares insights on sustainable hardware choices, emphasizing the benefits of keeping a smartphone as long as possible and opting for refurbished models, like the iPhone SE. Tips on recycling old devices and choosing environmentally friendly options like the Fairphone are also discussed. The key message is to prolong the life of gadgets to reduce e-waste and lower carbon emissions, while also saving money.

recent_posts.title: Education Needs Teachers, Not More Technology
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the complexities and stresses of integrating AI and multiple digital tools into education, arguing that while technology can aid teaching, it cannot replace the crucial role of teachers. The difficulty parents face in managing numerous educational apps for their children, and the flaws in current systems, are highlighted. The post underlines the importance of teacher involvement and the need for adequate tech-literacy skills for students, while criticizing the over-reliance on technology.

recent_posts.title: CSS Masonry Layout Syntax
recent_posts.summary: The CSS masonry layout syntax introduces a way to create masonry-style grid layouts in CSS without the need for Javascript libraries. This approach aims to overcome performance issues associated with JS and potentially revives the popularity of unique grid designs. The two main suggestions for integrating masonry into CSS are as part of Grid or as a separate layout method. The discussion also covers the appropriateness of the term 'masonry' in this context.
